nodes.title: Circle-grid calibration (mono + stereo)
widgets_values:
Circle-grid calibration in two flavors (cv2.findCirclesGrid + cv2.calibrateCamera + cv2.stereoCalibrate).

SECTION A - detect: the flat 4x11 ASYMMETRIC target (staggered rows) is detected with CALIB_CB_ASYMMETRIC_GRID | CALIB_CB_CLUSTERING and the 44 centers are overlaid. A non-grid image yields found=false and an empty Nx1x2 array (a detection miss never halts the workflow).

SECTION B - MONO calibration: six posed, barrel-distorted views of the same target are batched and fed to 'Calibrate Camera (Circle Grid)', which recovers K (fx=fy~800) and distortion (k1<0). The distorted view 0 is then straightened with cv2.undistort using the recovered parameters. Compare the distorted input preview against the undistorted one: the straight vertical column of circles proves the correction.

SECTION C - STEREO calibration: the SAME six poses seen from two cameras 100 mm apart (left/right views). 'Stereo Calibrate (Circle Grid)' recovers the relative pose R~I, T~[-100,0,0] mm AND refines both cameras' intrinsics. This is the case where the ASYMMETRIC layout is load-bearing: a symmetric grid is identical under 180-degree rotation, so a tilted board cannot be matched unambiguously across two views; the staggered rows break that ambiguity. R/T feed cv2.stereoRectify -> cv2.initUndistortRectifyMap -> cv2.remap, whose output should show the board in the SAME place and orientation in both views (epipolar alignment), ready for disparity.

Try: replace the views with your own circle-grid photos; unplug K/dist from section B to see stereoCalibrate estimate intrinsics from scratch; feed 'cv2.stereoRectify' into a disparity node.
